s: Persistent and ephemeral memory systems that allow AI agents to retain context across interactions, learn from past experiences, and maintain coherent long-term state.
w: Agents accumulate memories across conversations and tasks. Short-term memory stores current conversation context (working memory buffer). Long-term memory persists facts, preferences, and learned patterns in vector stores or key-value databases. Episodic memory replays past interactions for few-shot retrieval. Semantic memory extracts generalized knowledge. Memory is indexed by recency, relevance, and importance scores to fit within context window limits.
use: Multi-turn conversational agents that need to recall prior interactions
Personalization systems remembering user preferences across sessions
Task-oriented agents building up knowledge over repeated workflows
Research agents accumulating findings across exploration steps
avoid: Simple single-turn Q&A where no state is needed
Scenarios where all context fits in the LLM context window natively
Privacy-sensitive domains without explicit memory retention controls

props.memory_window_size: Number of recent interactions retained in working memory
props.consolidation_interval: How often short-term memories are summarized into long-term storage
props.retrieval_top_k: Number of past memories retrieved per query

pat.d: Periodically summarize working memory into compressed long-term entries, pruning redundant or low-importance facts.
Retrieve from short-term (recency) and long-term (relevance) stores, merge and rank before injecting into context.

pits: Unbounded memory growth without pruning strategies - older entries become stale and consume retrieval bandwidth
Memory pollution from incorrect LLM-generated facts being persisted as truth
Retrieval latency adding unacceptable delay to conversational responses
Privacy leaks when agent memories contain sensitive data from other users
tips: Implement explicit user controls: view, edit, and delete memories for transparency
Use importance scoring (relevance + recency decay) rather than naive chronological retrieval
Separate working memory (fast, ephemeral) from long-term memory (slow, persistent) for clean architecture
